text: LiteRT-LM's litert::support::Tokenizer interface (support/tokenizer/tokenizer.h) declares TextToTokenIds, TokenToId (raw lookup, NotFound if absent), TokenIdsToText(ids, skip_special_tokens), GetTokens and GetVocabSize; TokenizerType has kUnspecified, kSentencePiece and kHuggingFace.

ModelResourcesLitertLm::GetTokenizer (LiteRT-LM agello-next) tries the SentencePiece tokenizer section first and the HuggingFace (HF_Tokenizer_Zlib) section second; if a section is found but its library was compiled out it returns Unimplemented, and if neither section exists it returns NotFound.

LitertLmLoader::GetSentencePieceTokenizer and GetHuggingFaceTokenizer look up the tokenizer section keyed by data type and lowercase model type, and for tf_lite_prefill_decode fall back to a tokenizer section without a model_type item; the HF_Tokenizer_Zlib section is decompressed into a new owning buffer.

In LiteRT-LM agello-next both tokenizer libraries are compiled in by default: //build_config:enable_huggingface_tokenizer is a bool_flag defaulting to True, //runtime/components:model_resources depends on //support/tokenizer:huggingface_tokenizer and :sentencepiece_tokenizer unless the disable flag or DISABLE_*_TOKENIZER define is set, and the build:agello config in .bazelrc sets neither.

The Gemma 4 .litertlm files documented in generated/models (E4B ours and Google's, E2B, E2B-gpu, E4B-gpu) and the EmbeddingGemma 2 text 270m file each have exactly one SP_Tokenizer section with no items (section 1) and no HF_Tokenizer_Zlib section; in our E4B file it spans bytes 32768 to 4721781 (4,689,013 bytes).

text: SentencePieceTokenizer::TokenIdsToText (LiteRT-LM) returns InvalidArgument when skip_special_tokens is true, NotFound for an ID outside [0, vocab size), and for a single control token (such as BOS or EOS) returns its piece via IdToPiece instead of decoding.
SentencePieceTokenizer::TokenToId returns NotFound when SentencePiece's PieceToId returns the unknown-token ID.

LiteRT-LM's HuggingFaceTokenizer is built on the tokenizers_cpp C API (include/tokenizers_c.h from @tokenizers_cpp), is created from a JSON string with tokenizers_new_from_str, and encodes with add_special_tokens = 0.

BufferedStreamingDetokenizer::ProcessStep re-decodes all accumulated token IDs of a head each step, trims trailing U+FFFD replacement characters, and releases only the not-yet-released part of the longest common prefix of the previous and current decodes, cut back so it never ends inside a valid multi-byte UTF-8 sequence; on the first decode with text it releases nothing (one-step lag).

BufferedStreamingDetokenizer keeps lookback_tokens (default 8) already-released tokens per head; once more are released it erases the older ones from the accumulated IDs and re-decodes the remaining window to resynchronize the released length.

In DecodeOneStep::Run (runtime/core/tasks.cc) each step's sampled tokens pass through StopTokenStreamFilter::ProcessStep before BufferedStreamingDetokenizer::ProcessStep; the filter buffers tokens that may start a stop sequence and discards the tokens of a completed stop sequence, so stop tokens are not detokenized.

In LiteRT-LM agello-next, Tasks::Decode (runtime/core/tasks.cc) gets the vocabulary size for the thinking-budget constraint from tokenizer.GetVocabSize() (Agello commit 5e946049, comment 'Agello (T2)') instead of building every token's string.

StopTokenDetector::ProcessTokens keeps a match length per batch row and stop sequence: a token equal to the next expected token advances it; any other token resets it to 1 if it equals the sequence's first token, else to 0 (no fallback to a shorter partial match).
StopTokenDetector::AddStopTokenSequence returns InvalidArgument for an empty sequence and ignores a sequence that was already added.

SessionConfig::MaybeUpdateAndValidate copies the LlmMetadata stop_tokens that have token IDs when the session config has no stop token IDs; EngineSettings::MaybeUpdateAndValidate converts stop tokens given as token_str to IDs with the tokenizer (TokenToId first, TextToTokenIds if that fails).

The LlmMetadata of the Gemma 4 E4B (ours and Google's), E2B and both -gpu .litertlm files lists start_token ID 2 and stop_tokens IDs 1, 50 and 106; google/gemma-4-E4B-it's generation_config.json lists bos_token_id 2 and eos_token_id [1, 106, 50].

text: LiteRT-LM's Sampler interface (runtime/components/sampler.h) has SampleToIdAndScoreBuffer(logits, ids, scores) and UpdateConfig(params, batch, rng), plus optional CanHandleInput, HandlesInput and SetInferenceFuncAndInputTensors for samplers that also prepare the next decode's inputs.

CreateSampler(Backend::GPU, ...) in LiteRT-LM agello-next calls CreateGpuSampler; it returns the result on success or on any error other than kUnavailable, and on kUnavailable logs 'GPU sampler unavailable. Falling back to CPU sampling.' and falls through to CreateCpuSampler (Agello adds telemetry counters and a sampler fact there).

On Apple (#if defined(__APPLE__) in CreateGpuSampler, runtime/components/sampler_factory.cc), LiteRT-LM tries the Metal TopK sampler only when the LiteRT environment options contain a kMetalDevice option and no kWebGpuDevice option.

TopKMetalCApiSampler::Create first loads libLiteRtTopKMetalSampler.dylib with SharedLibrary::Load (RTLD lazy, local) and looks up the LiteRtTopKMetalSampler_* C functions; if loading fails with kUnavailable it uses the statically linked function pointers LiteRtTopKMetalSampler_*_Static, which are declared with a nullptr default, and returns Unavailable when any of them is null.

In the LiteRT-LM source at both agello-next 7b872544 and v0.18.0, the Bazel target //runtime/components:default_static_gpu_samplers has empty deps in every select branch, so no GPU (Metal) sampler implementation is linked from the open source.

In the iOS arm64 slices compared in generated/binaries.md, Google's prebuilt v0.18.0 CLiteRTLM has 39 defined symbols and 25 string mentions matching the TopK Metal sampler, against 7 defined and 25 in strings for our agello-next build.

text: CreateCpuSampler (runtime/components/sampler_factory.cc) returns a TopPSampler for SamplerParameters::TOP_P, nullptr for TYPE_UNSPECIFIED (the executor then handles sampling), and UnimplementedError for any other type, including TOP_K and GREEDY.

The LiteRT-LM Swift wrapper creates sampler parameters with kLiteRtLmSamplerTypeTopP whenever a SamplerConfig is given, while the C API's ToSamplerParametersType maps kLiteRtLmSamplerTypeTopK and kLiteRtLmSamplerTypeGreedy to SamplerParameters TOP_K and GREEDY.
TopPSampler::Create returns InvalidArgument for k <= 0, p outside [0, 1], a non-positive batch or sequence size, or a negative temperature.

LiteRT-LM's CPU TopKTopPSampling (runtime/components/sampling_cpu_util.cc) with k == 1 returns the argmax token (found with MaxElement) with probability 1, so p and temperature don't affect it; with k > 1 it takes the top k, softmaxes them at the temperature, keeps the smallest prefix of the sorted candidates whose cumulative probability reaches p, and draws uniformly within that mass.

In LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorStatic::Create, both in agello-next and in v0.18.0, the decode signature's logits output gets an FP16 tensor buffer (CreateFP16OutputBuffer) when use_fp16_precision (FP16 activation type, the default, on the GPU backend) is true and GetSamplerBackend returns Backend::GPU; otherwise it uses the compiled model's own output buffer. The condition is the configured sampler backend, not whether a GPU sampler library loads.

text: GetSamplerBackend (runtime/executor/llm_executor_settings_utils.cc) returns the executor's sampler backend, or when it is UNSPECIFIED the main backend (CPU for NPU); LlmExecutorSettings leaves it UNSPECIFIED unless a sampler backend is passed, and the C API's EngineSettings::CreateDefault call passes none. When it is GPU, the GPU compilation options also mark 'logits' as an external tensor.

With FP16 logits, the v0.18.0 TopPSampler reads them into a new uint16 vector and converts every value to float32 before sampling; agello-next's TopPSampler (Agello commit fdd5bac7) reads them into a reused member vector and, when k == 1 and exact log-probs aren't requested with scores, picks the first maximum of each row by comparing the half-precision bit patterns as integers without conversion, falling back to the float path if the maximum is a NaN.

text: Agello's GreedyHalf maps a half h to (h & 0x8000) ? ~h : (h | 0x8000) so integer order matches value order, takes the first maximum, returns -1 when it is a NaN, and when the maximum is a zero returns the first +0 or -0 in the row.
On agello-next's greedy FP16 path, TopPSampler writes a score of 0.0 (the log of probability 1) for each row when a scores tensor is given.

The MTP drafter (runtime/executor/llm_litert_mtp_drafter.cc) creates its drafter and verifier samplers with CreateGreedySampler: SamplerParameters TOP_P, k 1, p 0, temperature 1, seed 0, through CreateSampler with the main backend, so on a GPU engine without a GPU sampler they fall back to the CPU TopPSampler like the main sampler.
LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorBase::InitializeSampler replaces TYPE_UNSPECIFIED sampler params with TOP_P, k 1, p 0, temperature 1, seed 0.

text: LiteRT-LM's logit masks: MaskType is kBitmap, kSparse, kComposite or kCustom; a BitmapLogitMask stores ceil(vocab/64) 64-bit words (bit set = allowed) and sets disallowed logits, and logits past vocab_size, to -infinity for FP32 or tflite::half::min() for FP16; a SparseLogitMask applies z' = z*w + b per entry (dividing negative logits by w when sign_dependent_weight) and skips logits already at -infinity or half::min(); a CompositeLogitMask fuses its bitmaps with a bitwise AND, then applies custom masks, then sparse ones.

FP16 logit masks in LiteRT-LM set disallowed logits to the most negative finite half, -65504 (tflite::half::min() is from_bits(0xfbff); the mask runner's kDisallowedBiasF16 is -65504), not to -infinity; FP32 masks use -infinity.
BitmapLogitMask::Apply also disallows logits at indices >= vocab_size (padding), clamping a negative vocab_size to 0.

ConstrainedDecoder::ProcessLogits in agello-next requires logits of shape [batch, 1, vocab] matching its batch size, computes one mask per row with Constraint::ComputeMask and applies them through LiteRtLogitMaskRunner::ApplyBatch.

Agello commit ef197a04 in agello-next: BitmapLogitMask::CreateAllAllowed sets an all_allowed_ flag, and LiteRtLogitMaskRunner::ApplySlices treats a bitmap mask with that flag whose vocab_size covers the logits' vocabulary as no mask, returning without touching the logits when every row's mask is then null.

LiteRtLogitMaskRunner::ApplySlices (agello-next) masks a kHostMemory logits buffer in place on the CPU; otherwise, when created for an accelerator other than kNone, it unpacks the masks into bias/weight staging tensors and runs a lazily compiled LiteRT graph (one of seven GraphKind variants) on that accelerator; custom masks and nested composites fall back to reading the logits to the host, masking and writing them back.

On a GPU engine, DecodeOneStep::Create builds the ConstrainedDecoder with the executor's LiteRT environment and GetHwAcceleratorForBackend(GPU) = HwAccelerators::kGpu, and the FP16 decode logits buffer is created with the first buffer type in the compiled model's output requirements rather than host memory, so non-trivial masks run as LiteRT graphs on the GPU accelerator; the runner's GPU options mark 'logits' and 'masked_logits' as external tensors and set FP16 or FP32 precision by the logits' element type.

In LiteRT-LM v0.18.0 (what Agello ships) there is no LiteRtLogitMaskRunner: ConstrainedDecoder::ProcessLogits masks host-memory logits in place and, for any other buffer type (GPU), copies the logits to a host vector with CopyFromTensorBuffer, masks them and writes them back.
ConstrainedDecoder::UpdateState advances each row's constraint state with ComputeNext(state, token) and restarts it with Start() when the constraint reports IsEnded.

LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorBase::DecodeLogitsImpl updates the constrained decoder's state with the step's input token IDs only when the previous run was a decode, then calls ProcessLogits on the output logits inside the kConstraint telemetry span.
LlmLiteRtMtpDrafter creates two LiteRtLogitMaskRunners (drafter and verifier) for GetHwAcceleratorForBackend of its backend.
LiteRT-LM's Constraint interface has Start(), IsEnded(state), GetVocabularySize(), ComputeNext(state, token) and ComputeMask(state) (default: wraps the deprecated ComputeBitmap in a BitmapLogitMask).

DecodeOneStep::Create (runtime/core/tasks.cc) builds one CompositeConstraint per decode turn: a RepetitionPenaltyConstraint, NoRepeatNgramConstraint and SuppressTokensConstraint when their configs are enabled (owned), then the caller's constraint, if any, as an unowned member; with no members no ConstrainedDecoder is created.

CompositeConstraint::AddConstraint rejects a member whose vocabulary size differs from the composite's, IsEnded returns true as soon as any member's state is ended, and ComputeMask returns a CompositeLogitMask of the members' masks.

Because CompositeConstraint::IsEnded is true when any member ends and ConstrainedDecoder::UpdateState then calls Start() on the whole composite, the end of one member (for example a finished response-format constraint) resets every member's state, including repetition-penalty token counts.

Tasks::Decode wraps the caller's constraint in a ThinkingBudgetConstraint whenever the thinking token budget has a value other than 0 and the thinking end token IDs are non-empty; a budget of -1 means no limit but still suspends the wrapped constraint while the model thinks.

Conversation::CreateDecodeConfig sets the thinking budget from ThinkingConfig when thinking is enabled, the start IDs by tokenizing the first channel's start string (empty when that channel is already open) and the end IDs from its end string; with thinking disabled it sets the budget to 0.

ThinkingBudgetConstraint::ComputeMask returns: at step 0 the wrapped constraint's mask plus the first start token (all allowed without a wrapped constraint); after a partial start match only the next start token; while thinking within budget an all-allowed bitmap; after CheckBudget triggers (thinking_token_count >= budget, budget >= 0) only the next end token; in the content phase the wrapped constraint's mask.

ThinkingBudgetConstraint leaves the thinking phase when the model itself generates the full end-token sequence (ProcessNaturalEnd), and IsEnded is true only in the content phase when the wrapped constraint has ended.

RepetitionPenaltyConfig clamps repetition_penalty to >= 1 and window_size to >= 0 and is enabled when the penalty exceeds 1 or presence or frequency penalty is non-zero; RepetitionPenaltyConstraint's mask is a sparse mask with, for each token counted in the window, weight 1/penalty applied sign-dependently and bias -(presence_penalty + count * frequency_penalty).

RepetitionPenaltyConstraint counts generated tokens; with window_size > 0 it keeps a ring buffer of that many tokens and decrements the count of the token that leaves it; window_size 0 counts the whole turn.

NoRepeatNgramConfig raises a non-zero window_size below the n-gram size to the n-gram size; NoRepeatNgramConstraint's mask allows everything until n tokens were generated, then disallows the tokens that followed the current (n-1)-token prefix earlier.
With window_size 0, NoRepeatNgramConstraint appends every token to its state's token_history, and ComputeNext copies the whole state each step.
SuppressTokensConstraint precomputes one bitmap disallowing the configured token IDs; SessionConfig takes suppress tokens from LlmMetadata.suppress_tokens when the file has any.

LiteRT-LM's legacy ModelType enum (runtime/components/model_resources.h) has kTfLitePrefillDecode, kTfLiteEmbedder, kTfLitePerLayerEmbedder, kTfLiteAux, kTfLiteAudioFrontend, kTfLiteAudioEncoderHw, kTfLiteAudioAdapter, kTfLiteEndOfAudio, kTfLiteVisionAdapter, kTfLiteEndOfVision, kTfLiteVisionEncoder, kArtisanTextDecoder, kTfLiteMtpDrafter, kTfLiteMtpAux and kTfLiteTextEncoder, and is marked deprecated in favor of the capability-scoped proto enums.
ModelResources creates each model lazily on first Get*() call, reuses it afterwards, and is documented as not thread-safe.

ModelResourcesLitertLm::GetTFLiteModel caches models by lowercase model-type string; with file-backed loading enabled it creates the litert::Model with Model::CreateFromFd over the section range of a duplicated descriptor, otherwise with Model::CreateFromBuffer over the loader's mapped section buffer.

EngineAdvancedImpl::Create enables file-backed model loading only for the NPU backend with magic-number configuration off (comment: magic-number replacement mutates the model flatbuffer in place), and BuildModelResourcesFromLitertLmFormat otherwise enables it only for AOT NPU files with a non-empty TF_LITE_AUX section; a GPU or CPU engine builds its models from the mapped section buffers.
ModelResourcesLitertLm::GetLlmMetadata parses the LlmMetadataProto section on first use and caches it, returning Internal on a parse failure.

In both LiteRT-LM agello-next and v0.18.0, ResourceManager::CreateContextHandler returns InvalidArgument 'Lora is not supported.' when the session config carries a scoped (text) LoRA file that isn't already loaded, and no code path loads one; only an audio LoRA is loaded, into the audio encoder's LoraManager.
The C function litert_lm_session_config_set_lora_path rejects a null or empty path, opens the file as a ScopedFile and stores it as the session config's scoped LoRA file.

LiteRT-LM LoRA weights are read as a TFLite flatbuffer (FlatBufferLoraData), LoraManager loads and selects them per LoRA ID for a compiled model signature, and GPU models exported with runtime-BMM LoRA take a 'lora_param_tensor' input.

EmbeddingLookupText::Initialize compiles the embedder model with HwAccelerators::kCpu on every non-Android platform (NPU then CPU on Android), so on iOS and macOS text and per-layer embeddings are computed on the CPU, with one CompiledModel::Run per token in LookupInternal.

EmbeddingLookupText requires an FP32 output, computes floats per token as the product of output dimensions from index 2, computes the embedding of token 0 at initialization, and uses it for negative token IDs and for padding rows after the last token in LookupPrefill.

EmbeddingLookupManager::LookupDecode returns InvalidArgument 'Multimodal embeddings are not supported during decode.' for negative token IDs; LookupPrefill writes the text embeddings first and then lets each multimodal and end-of-multimodal lookup overwrite its slots.
LiteRT-LM uses placeholder token IDs ExecutorVisionData::kSpecialToken -1 and kEndToken -3, and ExecutorAudioData::kSpecialToken -2 and kEndToken -4.

EmbeddingLookupMultiModal copies the next floats-per-token values from its locked embedding buffer into each slot whose token equals its special token, consuming the buffer in order; UpdateMultiModalEmbeddings adds one lookup for vision (-1) and one for projected audio (-2) embeddings per prefill.
EndOfMultiModalEmbedding requires a model with one signature, no inputs and one FP32 output; it compiles it for the CPU outside Android, runs it once at initialization and caches the output.

InitializeEmbeddingLookups maps the end-of-audio and end-of-vision sections to kEndToken -4 and -3, creates the embedder's manager with multimodal support and the per-layer embedder's without it, and passes each its external-weight resources.

In our Gemma 4 E4B file (gemma-4-E4B-it-fp16-rope.litertlm), the tf_lite_embedder signature 'embedder' takes token_ids INT32[1, 1] and returns embeddings FLOAT32[1, 1, 2560]; the end-of-audio and end-of-vision sections are signatures 'eoa' and 'eoi' with 0 ops, no inputs and one FLOAT32[1, 1, 2560] output.

text: In LiteRT-LM agello-next, //support/preprocessor:image_preprocessor resolves to the stb implementation unless --define enable_skia_image_preprocessor=true (build:agello doesn't set it), and the audio preprocessor depends on @miniaudio//:miniaudio_objc on iOS and macOS (plain @miniaudio elsewhere).

AudioPreprocessorConfig::CreateDefaultGemma4Config is 16 kHz mono, frame 320 and hop 160 samples (640 and 640 when mel extraction is skipped), FFT 512, 128 mel bins from 0 to 8000 Hz, mel floor 1e-3, periodic Hanning window, centered FFT padding; Gemma4DataProcessor uses it.
AudioPreprocessorMiniAudio decodes WAV, FLAC and MP3 with miniaudio and supports only mono audio.

Gemma4DataProcessor patchifies images with the patch width, height, max_num_patches and pooling kernel size of its config; the stb preprocessor decodes with stbi_load_from_memory and resizes keeping the aspect ratio to fit max_num_patches; our E4B file's metadata has patch_width 16, patch_height 16, max_num_patches 2520.

sources.detail: Metadata text: gemma4 { patch_width: 16 patch_height: 16 max_num_patches: 2520 }

text: A .litertlm file starts with the 8-byte magic 'LITERTLM', three little-endian uint32 version numbers (major, minor, patch), 4 bytes of padding, a little-endian uint64 header end offset at byte 24, and the LiteRTLMMetaData flatbuffer from byte 32 to that offset (ReadHeaderFromLiteRTLM; Python builder constants HEADER_END_LOCATION_BYTE_OFFSET 24 and HEADER_BEGIN_BYTE_OFFSET 32).

ReadHeaderFromLiteRTLM, in both agello-next and v0.18.0, returns Unimplemented when the file's major version differs from LITERTLM_MAJOR_VERSION (1) and never compares the minor or patch version, so any 1.x.y container is accepted at the header level.
LITERTLM_MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH_VERSION are 1.9.0 in LiteRT-LM agello-next and 1.7.0 in v0.18.0, and the Python litert_lm_builder writes version 1.9.0.

Container versions and header end offsets of the files in generated/models: gemma-4-E4B-it-fp16-rope (ours), gemma-4-E4B-it and gemma-4-E2B-it are 1.5.0 with header end 1,872; gemma-4-E4B-it-gpu and gemma-4-E2B-it-gpu are 1.6.0 with 704; embeddinggemma-2-text-270m is 1.7.0 with 880.

LitertLmLoader::Initialize maps and parses at most the first kLitertLmHeaderMaxSize = 16 * 1024 bytes of the file, so a header whose end offset exceeds 16,384 makes ReadHeaderFromLiteRTLM fail ('Failed to read header data.') through this loader.

The schema comment and the Python builder place each section at the next multiple of BLOCK_SIZE = 16 * 1024 after the previous section's end (the first after 32 + metadata size); all six files in generated/models have every section begin on a 16,384-byte boundary immediately after the previous end rounded up.

sources.detail: header.sections[*].begin all multiples of 16384; first begin 16384; each begin = round_up(previous end, 16384)

text: In schema/core/litertlm_header_schema.fbs, LiteRTLMMetaData holds SystemMetadata (KeyValuePair entries) and SectionMetadata (SectionObject list); a SectionObject has optional KeyValuePair items, begin_offset and end_offset (ulong, range [begin, end)) and an AnySectionDataType; KeyValuePair values are a VData union of UInt8, Int8, UInt16, Int16, UInt32, Int32, Float32, Bool, StringValue, UInt64, Int64 and Double.

AnySectionDataType (ubyte) in agello-next lists, in order: NONE, GenericBinaryData, Deprecated, TFLiteModel, SP_Tokenizer, LlmMetadataProto, HF_Tokenizer_Zlib, TFLiteWeights, EmbeddingMetadataProto, ExecutorMetadataProto, TtsMetadataProto, AsrMetadataProto, Text2ImageMetadataProto.

ExtractBufferKeyAndTfLiteSectionHint keys TFLiteModel, TFLiteWeights, SP_Tokenizer and HF_Tokenizer_Zlib sections by data type plus the lowercase model_type item, GenericBinaryData by its 'name' item and other types by data type alone; a TFLiteModel or TFLiteWeights section without model_type is keyed as tf_lite_prefill_decode with a warning; it also collects backend_constraint and prefer_activation_type items (keys matched case-insensitively).

LitertLmLoader accepts a model_type string only if, uppercased, it parses as a non-unspecified value of LlmMetadata, EmbeddingMetadata, TtsMetadata, AsrMetadata or Text2ImageMetadata TfLiteModelType, or as a legacy ModelType string; otherwise Initialize fails with InvalidArgument 'Unknown model type: ...'.

LitertLmLoader::Initialize stores each section's hint and [begin, end) range in unordered_maps keyed by BufferKey (data type + lowercase model_type) by assignment, so when two sections share a key the later one in header order replaces the earlier; the loader never chooses among duplicate sections by backend_constraint or prefer_activation_type.

In the LLM engine, section hints are used once, in EngineSettings::MaybeUpdateAndValidate, and only for tf_lite_prefill_decode (Main), tf_lite_vision_encoder (Vision) and tf_lite_audio_encoder_hw (Audio): ValidateBackendConstraint splits backend_constraint on ',' and compares each part case-insensitively with GetBackendString of the executor's backend, returning InvalidArgument '... backend constraint mismatch' if none matches; no constraint passes.

MaybeOverrideActivationType applies a section's prefer_activation_type only when the executor settings have no activation data type: fp32/float32/fp32_fp16 map to FLOAT32 (fp32_fp16 also enables mixed precision), fp16/float16 to FLOAT16, int16 and int8 to INT16 and INT8, anything else is InvalidArgument.

Potential mismatch found by reading code: the Python builder validates backend_constraint after splitting on ',' and stripping spaces but stores the original string lowercased (its docstring example is 'cpu, gpu'), while the runtime's ValidateBackendConstraint splits on ',' without trimming, so a stored ' gpu' part would not match a GPU executor backend.

In the Gemma 4 E4B (ours and Google's) and E2B .litertlm files, tf_lite_audio_encoder_hw, tf_lite_audio_adapter and tf_lite_vision_adapter carry backend_constraint=cpu, tf_lite_vision_encoder and tf_lite_prefill_decode carry prefer_activation_type=fp16, and the embedder, per-layer embedder, end-of-audio, end-of-vision and MTP drafter sections carry neither.

EngineSettings::CreateDefault creates the vision executor settings with adapter_backend CPU (comment 'Vision adapter can only run on CPU') and the audio executor settings with adapter_backend CPU, independent of the file's backend constraints.

EngineSettings::CreateDefault switches a GPU engine (and a GPU audio backend) to Backend::GPU_ARTISAN when the file has a TFLiteModel section with model_type tf_lite_artisan_text_decoder, and the open CreateLlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutor returns InvalidArgument 'Unsupported backend' for any backend other than CPU, GPU and NPU, so the documented build can't run the -gpu files; Google's v0.18.0 binary has 166 defined GPU-artisan-executor symbols against 29 in ours.

text: gemma-4-E4B-it-gpu.litertlm and gemma-4-E2B-it-gpu.litertlm (litert-community revisions 2eee7ac3 and b3ca0d2f) are container 1.6.0 with three sections: LlmMetadataProto, SP_Tokenizer and one TFLiteModel with model_type tf_lite_artisan_text_decoder, backend_constraint gpu_artisan and gpu_artisan_weights_version 0.0 (2,964.3 MB for E4B, 2,003.7 MB for E2B).

text: LitertLmLoader::GetSectionBuffer maps a section lazily on first request under a mutex and caches its BufferRef; with a ScopedFile source MapSection memory-maps from the begin offset rounded down to MemoryMappedFile::GetOffsetAlignment() (getpagesize() on POSIX) and points the buffer past the gap, and with an already memory-mapped file it uses pointer arithmetic.
LiteRT-LM's POSIX MemoryMappedFile::Create maps with PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE and MAP_PRIVATE, then calls madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) under #ifdef __APPLE__ (MADV_WILLNEED on other platforms).

litert_lm_engine_settings_create builds ModelAssets from the path; ModelAssets opens it as a ScopedFile; GetFileFormat trusts the .tflite/.task/.litertlm extension and otherwise checks the first 8 bytes for TFL3, PK or a LITERTLM prefix; BuildLiteRtCompiledModelResources accepts only the TASK and LITERT_LM formats.

EngineAdvancedImpl::Create sends model assets backed by a data stream through CreateStreamingWeights (the streaming loader, which reads sections in file order without memory-mapping); on Emscripten a GPU engine whose model has external weights is upgraded to that path.
BuildModelResourcesFromTaskFormat opens a .task (ZIP) bundle with ModelAssetBundleResources and requires a TF_LITE_PREFILL_DECODE entry.

The litert-community Hugging Face repositories gemma-4-E4B-it-litert-lm and gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm (main, listed 2026-10-15) contain .litertlm, -gpu.litertlm, -web.litertlm and -web.task files; E2B also has Google Tensor, Intel and Qualcomm specific .litertlm files; the -web.litertlm and -gpu.litertlm files have the same byte size (2,969,059,328 for E4B, 2,008,432,640 for E2B).

LlmMetadata (runtime/proto/llm_metadata.proto) fields: start_token 1, stop_tokens 2, prompt_templates 3, sampler_params 4, max_num_tokens 5, llm_model_type 6, jinja_prompt_template 7, channels 8, suppress_tokens 9, kv_cache_init_value 10, supports_thinking 11, supports_function_calling 12, pad_token 13, min_runtime_version 14.

The LlmMetadata of the Gemma 4 E4B (ours and Google's) and E2B files has start token 2, stop tokens 1/50/106, a gemma4 llm_model_type (image and audio delimiter tokens, tool-call fences, patch 16x16, max_num_patches 2520), a Jinja prompt template and one channel 'thought' (start '<|channel>thought\n', end '<channel|>'), and no sampler_params, max_num_tokens or min_runtime_version; EmbeddingGemma 2's EmbeddingMetadata has embedding_gemma_v2, bos 2, eos 1, a miniaudio audio_preprocessor and max_input_length 1024.

LlmMetadata.TfLiteModelType values: TF_LITE_PREFILL_DECODE 1, EMBEDDER 2, PER_LAYER_EMBEDDER 3, AUX 4, AUDIO_ENCODER_HW 5, END_OF_AUDIO 6, VISION_ADAPTER 7, VISION_ENCODER 8, AUDIO_FRONTEND 9, AUDIO_ADAPTER 10, ARTISAN_TEXT_DECODER 11, END_OF_VISION 12, MTP_DRAFTER 13, MTP_AUX 14 (16-19 reserved); EmbeddingMetadata.TfLiteModelType starts with TF_LITE_TEXT_ENCODER 1.

ExecutorMetadata (llm_executor_metadata: max_history_size, state_buffers, attention_mask_settings) is optional: the LLM executor uses it only when GetExecutorMetadata succeeds; none of the files in generated/models has an ExecutorMetadataProto section.

embeddinggemma-2-text-270m.litertlm has six sections: EmbeddingMetadataProto, SP_Tokenizer, TFLiteModel tf_lite_embedder (3.1 MB), TFLiteModel tf_lite_text_encoder (21.3 MB), TFLiteWeights tf_lite_embedder (67.1 MB) and TFLiteWeights tf_lite_text_encoder (68.4 MB).

Weight placement in the files in generated/models: our E4B tf_lite_prefill_decode section has a 63.1 MB graph and 2,197.9 MB of weights after the graph in the same section; the other E4B sections the generator parsed (all but the per-layer embedder) and every E2B section keep weights inline; EmbeddingGemma 2 keeps 67.1 MB (embedder) and 68.4 MB (text encoder) in TFLiteWeights sections.

text: GetExternalWeightResources returns a duplicated file descriptor and a single region named 'tflite_weights' (offset, length) when a TFLiteWeights section exists for the model type, and nothing when it doesn't; SetExternalWeightOptions passes it to LiteRT with SetExternalWeightScopedFile, and the LLM executor calls it for kTfLitePrefillDecode.
EngineSettings::MaybeUpdateAndValidate only logs a warning when LlmMetadata.min_runtime_version is newer than LITERT_LM_VERSION.

An HF_Tokenizer_Zlib section begins with a little-endian uint64 uncompressed size, which DecompressData caps at 1 GB before zlib uncompress; the builder compresses a JSON tokenizer with zlib.compress.

LitertLmFileBuilder._build_sections packs the metadata with placeholder offsets to learn its size, writes each section starting at round_up(32 + metadata size, 16384) and then at the next 16,384-byte boundary after each section, then seeks to 0 and writes the magic, version 1.9.0, padding to byte 24, the header end offset and the final metadata.
The Python builder's Backend values are cpu, gpu, npu and gpu_artisan, and add_tflite_model stores backend_constraint and prefer_activation_type as lowercased string items.
litertlm_peek_main is run with 'bazel run //python/litert_lm_builder:litertlm_peek_main -- --litertlm_file=<file>' and accepts --dump_files_dir to dump sections.

GetModelInfo (schema/model_info) reads the header from a stream and classifies the file as an embedding model when it has EmbeddingMetadata, or a text encoder without LLM metadata or a main graph; it fills the LLM capability (modalities, thinking and tool support, speculative decoding, vision budgets, default sampler parameters, backends per modality, minimum runtime version, maximum context) when LlmMetadata exists or the file isn't an embedding model; for the main LLM graph the last kMainLlm section wins.

LitertLmLoader::GetLlmMetadata() calls .value() on the optional section buffer without checking it, and EngineAdvancedImpl::Create calls ModelResourcesLitertLm::GetLlmMetadata unconditionally, so an LLM engine created from a file without an LlmMetadataProto section fails on that optional access instead of returning a status.
The LiteRT-LM Swift wrapper creates engine settings with litert_lm_engine_settings_create and a model path.

gemma-4-E4B-it-fp16-rope.litertlm (ours, sha256 6353a233…) and Google's gemma-4-E4B-it.litertlm (sha256 0b2a8980…) share container version 1.5.0, header end 1,872, system metadata and the begin offsets of sections 0-10; section 10 (tf_lite_prefill_decode) is 2,261,026,416 bytes in ours against 2,260,043,376 (+983,040) and section 11 (tf_lite_mtp_drafter) 45,339,152 against 45,126,160 (+212,992).

Our E4B file is 3,660,726,272 bytes and its last section ends at 3,660,714,512 (11,760 bytes of trailing padding to a 16 KiB multiple); the -gpu and EmbeddingGemma files end exactly at their last section's end.
